newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec natgas prices rally again on storage-NGC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec natgas prices rally again on storage-NGC.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for December jumped sharply from November levels, driven by concerns about low Western storage and some colder-than-normal temperatures, Natural Gas Clearinghouse (NGC) said Friday.
U.S. spot gas prices for December averaged $3.70 per million British thermal units, up $1.09 for the month and the highest average price on record in the 11-year history of the NGC survey.
Prices into Columbia Gas rose $1.15 on the month to $3.80, about $1.60 over last year's levels, NGC said in its monthly survey.
Most Gulf pipes gained $1.05-1.15 for the month and jumped to about $1.50-1.60 above year-ago.
The largest monthly gain was at Texas Gas Transmission's Zone 1 in northern Louisiana, which surged $1.20 to $3.85, about $1.60 over the same year-ago month.
On Texas Eastern in Texas, December prices rose $1.05 to $3.70, about $1.60 over 1995 levels.
Oklahoma prices also were up $1.05-1.10 for the month, with sales into ANR in Custer County, Okla., averaging $3.65, $1.10 above last year's levels.

Prices represent NGC estimates of the median price for one month spot transactions at the indicated receipt points. The estimates are based upon quotes by industial end-users and local distribution companies, NGC said.
